_comment: rent-watch criteria. JSON, not YAML — ruled 2026-08-07 (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q22). JSON has no comments, so any key beginning with an underscore is ignored by the loader; EVERY other unrecognised key is a hard error, which is what stops this convention from swallowing a typo. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: this used to say the values here were 'already public in prototype/sources.yaml'. That stopped being true when min_rooms, min_surface_m2 and max_rent_cc became measured decisions rather than inherited defaults. What still holds, and is the part that matters, is that the file carries NO name, employer, income figure or address — only preferences about flat size, price and area. For private tuning, copy this to config/rent/criteria.local.json (gitignored); it overrides field by field.
_communes: EMPTY = REGION MODE, ruled 2026-08-22: the name is not checked and `postcode_prefixes` below is the whole location filter, i.e. anywhere in Île-de-France as of 2026-08-22, when the region was widened from 78/95 to all eight departements on the developer's ruling. It replaces the ten-commune Boucle de Seine list (Q1, 2026-08-07), which was measured on live payloads that day and yielded ZERO matches across all four sources while 60 listings sat in those two departements. To go back to a named list, put the communes here — the ten were: Sartrouville, Houilles, Maisons-Laffitte, Bezons, Cormeilles-en-Parisis, Argenteuil, Le Vésinet, Chatou, Carrières-sur-Seine, Montesson. With a list, matching is on the listing's COMMUNE FIELD only, never as a substring of the description — the prototype searched the description too, so a Paris listing saying 'proche Chatou' passed. `commune_rank` below still orders the results either way, so region mode does NOT lose the preference for the Boucle de Seine; it only stops it being a hard reject.
_postcode_prefixes: In REGION MODE (empty `communes`) these are the ONLY location filter, and the loader refuses both being empty — that combination is the one shape of this config that fails open, and over-matching is invisible because it looks like a busy market. With a commune list they are an AND, not an OR: their job is then to reject a same-named commune elsewhere in France. WIDENED 2026-08-22 to all eight Île-de-France departements (75, 77, 78, 91, 92, 93, 94, 95) on the developer's ruling; it was 78/95. 92 has been here twice: removed on 2026-08-07 because with a commune list it could not match anything and so read as intent it did not have, and back now because in region mode a prefix IS the intent. `commune_rank` keeps the Boucle de Seine ordered first, so widening the region did not flatten the preference — a Seine-Saint-Denis flat matches and scores below a Sartrouville one. To narrow again, cut this list; nothing else has to change. One difference between the modes, and it is deliberate: with a list, a listing with NO postcode is not disqualified (unknown is not wrong, hard rule 9) because the name already matched; in region mode the postcode is the only evidence there is, so an unknown one is refused.
_min_rooms: Pièces, not chambres. T3, ruled 2026-08-22 — REVERSES the T4 of Q3 (2026-08-07). Measured that day on live payloads: of the 13 listings that got past the location filter, 10 were rejected here alone, and all 10 were under the rent ceiling (9 In'li LLI at 1017–1353 € CC, one CDC 82 m² at 1669 €). T4-or-larger at ≤1800 € CC did not exist across the four live sources. `min_surface_m2` below still rejects a genuinely small T3, so this stayed a real filter rather than becoming a firehose — at 50 m² since 2026-08-22, which is a floor a real T3 clears and a converted studio does not. An UNKNOWN room count does not disqualify — that is the prototype's `(l.rooms or 0) < min_rooms` bug, which rejects every listing that did not state a room count.
_min_surface_m2: 50 m² since 2026-08-22 (was 75). In region mode this and `min_rooms` are the only shape filters left, so it is what stops a T3 of 45 m² being offered as a family flat — the surface floor does the work the commune list used to do incidentally. An UNKNOWN surface is NOT a disqualification (hard rule 9): it loses the surface score component instead. Widening the region and lowering this together is deliberate — more places, smaller floor, tighter rent.
_max_rent_cc: CHARGES COMPRISES, hard cutoff, ruled 2026-08-07 (Q2). Every source is normalised to CC before comparison; a source that reports hors charges must declare `charges_included: false` in sources.json so the charges can be added. 1200 € since 2026-08-22, down from 1800 on the developer's ruling. All eight listings that matched under the old ceiling quoted 1258–1669 € CC, so none of them survives this — and the yield still went UP, to 83 matches out of 478, because the region and the surface floor moved in the same change and opened a pool the old criteria never looked at. Do not read the first fact as implying the second: a yield predicted from the previous filter's matches is a guess, and one poll on a throwaway RENT_SCOUT_DB measures it. A listing whose CC rent cannot be determined is not disqualified — it loses the rent-headroom score component instead, and says so in its reasons.
_exclude_patterns: THE MEUBLÉ NEGATION GUARD (Track 7-D, developer ruling 2026-09-08). `non meublé` was NOT rejected before this and is not rejected after it either — the guard changes NOTHING on the store, and saying so is the point rather than a disappointment. TRIALLED over all 3 377 stored rows as ruled: 152 rows match the meublé rule, 13 carry a negated meublé, and the two sets are DISJOINT — gained 0 / lost 0 / changed 0. The two exclusion lists were safe for DIFFERENT reasons and only one of them on purpose: `exclude_title_patterns` carries an explicit lookahead, while this list is safe only by ADJACENCY — a trigger word must sit immediately before `meuble` — which is why `location non meublée` escapes (`location` is not adjacent) and why the 8 In'li rows escape (their negation is about a KITCHEN, and `cuisine` is not a trigger). What was NOT safe is a negation on the OTHER side: `appartement meublé ou non` and `meublé : non` were rejected outright. THE SHAPE WAS MEASURED, NOT MIRRORED — copying the title list's `(?![^\n]{0,15}\b(?:non|pas|sans)\b)` over here OVER-guards, because `appartement meublé, pas de vis-à-vis` and `appartement meublée, non loin de la gare` are ordinary French on a genuinely furnished flat and a 15-character window lets both through. So the lookahead admits only the two shapes that are an ANSWER to the question, `ou non` and `: non`. Reversed by deleting the lookahead. --- Property KIND and letting KIND, never tenure. Tenure exclusion lives in Tenure::isExcluded() and is deliberately absent from config: a user-editable regex duplicating CLAUDE.md §1 would be a second, weaker copy of the one guarantee that must not be config-overridable. Patterns are PCRE fragments matched case-insensitively against ACCENT-FOLDED text, so write `meuble`, not `meublé` — the loader refuses an accented pattern rather than letting it silently never match. Matched against title AND description.
_min_price_per_m2: Track 1f. Below this many € CC per m², a listing is DOUBTFUL and goes to the digest — never rejected, because the discriminating sentence usually lives on a detail page this source structurally never reads. It catches a room in a shared flat advertised with the WHOLE flat's surface, and a surface read off the wrong thing (one real MATCH priced a 400 m² GARDEN). Both pass every numeric filter: each number is individually plausible and only their RATIO is not. DERIVED, not chosen: over the 1 392 stored listings that survive every OTHER exclusion, the cheapest are 3.00, 3.75 and 4.54 €/m², then a jump of 2.21 to 6.75 — by far the largest break anywhere in the tail (every other gap below the 12th percentile is <= 0.54). 5.5 sits inside that gap. It is NOT a percentile: p5 is 8.11, which would eat 113 rows including plausible ones. STATED COST: it does NOT catch the Champs-sur-Marne pair at 6.88 and 7.14 €/m² that motivated this, because they sit ABOVE the gap in dense data (6.75, 6.88, 7.14, 7.87 within 1.1 of each other) — a threshold reaching them has no support in the distribution and would start eating genuine listings. Re-derive it against `state/rent-watch.sqlite3` before moving it.
_exclude_title_patterns: Matched against the TITLE ONLY, and that is the point. KNOWN OVER-REJECTION SHAPE (round-3 panel, 2026-08-30, zero real occurrences in 1 600 stored titles): a flat title naming ONE room without a count — `Appartement 2 pièces avec grande chambre`, `T3 lumineux, belle chambre sur cour` — is excluded; the count lookbehinds reach one word back only. Left as is until a real title pays for it. THE ROOM PATTERN IS A NOUN, NOT A POSITION (2026-08-29): `^\s*chambre\b` read the room as the first word and three live titles defeated it in a week — a leading emoji (`✅ Chambre 10 min RER B`, pushed as a match), an adjective (`Confortable chambre individuelle`), a plural mid-title (`Belles chambres dans appartement lumineux`). The replacement matches `chambre(s)` anywhere UNLESS a count precedes it (a digit, or un/deux/trois/quatre/cinq/six), because a flat COUNTS its bedrooms and a room rental NAMES one. Measured over all 1 593 stored titles: 48 room rentals caught (the anchored form: 36), zero flats. `parking`, `box`, `garage`, `cave` and `bureau` are property types in a title and ordinary amenities in a description — 'T4 avec parking' is wanted, 'Parking en sous-sol' is not. Matching these against the description would drop every flat that has a parking space; not matching them at all would let a parking ad through, because a parking ad states no rooms and no surface and an unknown measurement is never a disqualification. Most are anchored at the start of the title, which is where a property type sits — but not all, and that is deliberate. While EVERY pattern was anchored, the title-only scope protected nothing a sabotage could disprove: a `^` with no `m` flag cannot match inside an appended description either way, so widening the scope was a semantic no-op and the guarantee was untestable. The unanchored entries are phrases unambiguous wherever they sit in a title (`loue parking`, `emplacement de stationnement`) and ordinary in a description ('emplacement de stationnement inclus'), which gives the scope something real to protect.
_commune_rank: 1 = most wanted. Drives score component S1 only; it never filters. In REGION MODE (empty `communes`) this is the only place the Boucle de Seine preference survives, which is why the loader stops requiring a rank to appear in `communes` when that list is empty — applied there, the check would reject every rank and force anyone widening to a departement to delete their ordering. With a NAMED commune list the check is back on: a rank for a commune that is filtered out is dead config.
_weights: spec/PROJECT_BRIEF.md §5, weights ruled 2026-08-07. Normalised, so a disabled component does not silently depress every score by its share. `high_floor_no_lift` was the one weight that had to be negative, and negatives are excluded from the normalising total: a penalty is subtracted from what a listing earned, not part of what it could earn. THE HEATING PENALTIES ARE THE SECOND AND THIRD OF THAT KIND (Track 7-A, developer ruling 2026-09-08: penalise individual heating severely, electric worst, gas less). They STACK — electric −35, gas −20, and a mode stated with no energy −20. SEVERITY AS A NUMBER RATHER THAN AN ADJECTIVE: `positiveTotal()` is 105 in production, so −20 is 19 points on the 0–100 scale, and re-judging all 1 261 stored MATCH snapshots shows −20 already takes EVERY individually-heated flat below `push_min_score: 55`. −30 and −40 were measured and buy NOTHING at that gate — they only reorder rows already under it — so a bigger number would be theatre. About a fifth of today's individual pushes move to the daily digest. AN UNSTATED ENERGY TAKES THE BASE PENALTY ONLY (ruled): an unstated energy is not electricity, and that is the largest single class in the store (101 rows, 24 matched). STATED COST: `chauffage` reaches the stored text of only three of the eight sources, and all 40 individually-heated matched flats are In'li — so this ranks In'li flats below portal flats for a fact the portals never state. That is hard rule 9 behaving correctly (unknown is not 'no'), not a defect to repair later. Reversed by setting both heating weights to 0.
_commute: Off until an IDFM/PRIM key exists (Q1). The loader refuses `enabled: true` with a commute weight of 0, and refuses a non-zero weight while disabled — either way the score would misreport. Turning it on means: set enabled, name the station, set max_minutes, and give weights.commute a value.
_freshness_minutes: A listing first seen within this window earns the full freshness bonus (S7). The brief notes good LLI units go within hours.
_notify: Routing, ruled 2026-08-07. Nothing is batched: the premise of the whole tool is that good stock goes within hours. `channels` ships as console only, because a channel needing a credential cannot be the default in a repo whose .env is not filled in — enabling ntfy or email without its credential is a startup refusal, never a silent no-op.

notify._push_min_score: A5 (Track 6, developer ruling 2026-09-05): a MATCH scoring below this is NOT pushed on its own — it waits for the daily digest and is announced there under its own heading, « vérifié, score bas », never mixed with the « à vérifier » tenure doubts. MEASURED before the ruling, over all 1046 stored MATCH snapshots re-judged offline under production's shape (commute 30 / 75 min): p10 23 · p50 40 · p90 54 · max 69, so 55 is the p90 — about one match in ten arrives individually, the rest once a day. A SEPARATE knob from high_priority_score on purpose: that one drives the `!!` marker (score AND confidence ≥ 80, calibrated 2026-08-26) and this one drives delivery; the developer chose the delivery gate and declined to move the weights. A rent drop lifting a rolled-up flat over this line is a promotion, pushed once (DIGEST < ROLLUP < MATCH is monotone in the store). Remove the key to push every match again.
